issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() should return a double, but the solution implementation declares and returns an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected return type and about whether fractional students-per-tutor should be represented. Tests or instructor expectations using the UML's double signature would not match the solution's int signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the UML by changing the method signature in Lecture to return double and compute the value using floating-point division, e.g. public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() { return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); } Alternatively, if an integer result is intended, update the problem statement/UML to indicate an int return type.
